answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with proof of sequential work: minting an identity requires completing a verifiable delay function that takes real wall-clock time and can't be parallelized, so no single machine can spawn thousands of fakes at once. Each identity is rooted in an unforgeable time cost, like a vine that must grow before it can bear weight. A hollow shell account with no such history earns no trust, and an attacker flooding the network finds each fake identity sending only a faint ripple, so a large forgery campaign costs real time, not just cheap parallel compute.
